newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia wants Mideast peace talks to reopen soon.
newsitem.headline: Russia wants Mideast peace talks to reopen soon.

text.p: Russia's Foreign Ministry, holding Israel largely responsible for the latest violence in the Middle East, said on Thursday talks should reopen as soon as possible.
"The recent events in Jerusalem can be explained mostly by the measures taken by Israel," foreign ministry spokesman Gennady Tarasov told a news briefing.
"Both sides should be very cautious in their actions, peace negotiations should be resumed. Now there is stalemate."
More than 70 people have been killed in violence sparked after Israel opened a second entrance to a tourist tunnel near Moslem holy sites in Jerusalem last week.

U.S. President Bill Clinton invited Israeli and Palestinian leaders to a summit in Washington but the meeting ended with little more than agreement to resume Israeli-Palestinian talks and a Clinton plea that the volatile region give peace a chance.
Russian officials had played down the importance of the Washington meeting saying it was limited in its decisions by a U.N. Security Council vote at the weekend.
A vote in the United Nations Security Council on Saturday called for the safety and protection of Palestinian civilians to be ensured. The United States abstained.
"The main thing is that both sides expressed a readiness to continue a dialogue," Tarasov said. "Certain progress was made and that momentum towards peace should be resumed."
